text:
Samir: Quick sanity check — I'm looking at committing GPU capacity for inference this quarter. US-WEST1 vs EU-WEST1: gross hourly cost per p3-equivalent looks ~ $2.40 vs $2.95 before discounts. Want advice on how to split commitments across regions (1yr vs 3yr, reserved vs convertible) given latency targets for EU customers.
Maya: do we have actual tail-latency requirements per region? if EU SLO is 80ms p95, we should keep some capacity local.
Samir: yes EU p95 80ms, US p95 60ms. Traffic split right now is ~70% US / 25% EU / 5% APAC.
Alex: on commitments — shorter 1yr gives flexibility for weight changes but 3yr has ~20% deeper discount for committed-use on our cloud plan. Convertible commitments cost ~5% more but let us move instance families.
Priya: also consider egress + cross-region peering. EU->US egress is adding ~0.08/GB on top of instance costs for cross-regional fallbacks. that matters for model-loading heavy workflows.
BillingBot: monthly_report: region-costs-2026-02.pdf uploaded to //gcs/redwood-billing/reports/region-costs-2026-02.pdf (see last section: reserved commitments ROI table).
Samir: thanks @BillingBot — I pulled the PDF. Key numbers: after committed discounts our effective US-WEST1 GPU-hour = $1.85 (1yr), EU-WEST1 = $2.30 (1yr). 3yr pushes to $1.60 / $2.00. So delta per GPU-hour ~ $0.40-$0.45.
Maya: quick calc: at 24/7 utilization one GPU-year = 24*365 = 8760 hours. delta ~$0.4 * 8760 = ~$3500/GPU-year extra in EU. multiply by planned fleet size.
Alex: but utilization won't be 100%. For inference fleet expected util is 40-60% steady. Use committed capacity to cover base load, keep burst on on-demand or spot.
Priya: question: are spots stable in EU for our instance types? last quarter spot reclaim rate in EU-WEST1 was 12% vs 6% in US-WEST1.
Samir: yep that's what I saw. So recommended approach: 1) buy 1yr commitments in both regions to cover base (roughly 50% of projected peak), 2) use flexible convertible commitments only for US if we expect model family changes, 3) keep a small dedicated reserved pool in EU for latency-sensitive customers, 4) rely on spot for non-latency workloads.
Alex: also vendor negotiation: ask for a blended committed SKU across regions — cloud rep sometimes gives additional credits if we commit X GPUs across multiple regions. could cut effective delta by ~10%.
Priya: don't forget networking choices: colocating model storage in EU with CDN reduces cross-region load. cost to run S3-equivalent in EU is slightly higher but offsets egress when models are loaded frequently.
Samir: can we get a simple sensitivity table? I'm thinking rows: commit % of base (30/50/70), columns: effective $/GPU-hour EU vs US and expected yearly delta.
Maya: I made a quick one — here's a paste from my calc:
```
Scenario A (50% base coverage): US effective = $1.73, EU effective = $2.15, delta per GPU-year = $3,900
Scenario B (30% base): US = $1.80, EU = $2.22, delta = $2,100
Scenario C (70% base): US = $1.60, EU = $2.00, delta = $5,500
```
Alex: those look reasonable. We should also include expected reclaim risk cost for spot fallback (probability * penalty of burst failure).
Priya: for EU customers where latency matters, convert some of the 1yr reserved to dedicated BareMetal-like instances (higher cost) if we need consistent tail latency — but only for top-tier customers.
InfraSRE: note — capacity provisioning lead time in EU can be 3-5 weeks for large contiguous GPU packs; in US we saw 1-2 weeks. that's a non-trivial operational risk if we try to shift capacity fast.
Samir: good catch — means we should overcommit base capacity in EU slightly to avoid backorder issues. maybe +10% buffer.
Maya: action items: 1) Samir to propose exact counts by region and commit term by EOD Friday; 2) Priya to attach spot reclaim and peering egress stats to the doc; 3) Alex to contact cloud rep about a cross-region blended commitment quote; 4) BillingBot to surface blended-credit options in the next invoice.
Samir: I'll draft the commit proposal. quick question for numbers: should I use utilization 50% for conservative ROI?
Alex: yes use 50% and show 30/50/70 sensitivity.
Priya: I'll upload the spot/reclaim spreadsheet to the thread when ready.
Maya: approved as plan, +1 on buffer in EU.
Samir: thanks everyone — will post the proposal here.
